title: Sensing chemistry: the EC cell relay
objective: Explain how enterochromaffin cells let afferents sense luminal chemistry.

steps.title: A sensor cell in the lining
steps.body: Afferent endings often don't touch the lumen directly. Instead, specialized **[[enterochromaffin cell|enterochromaffin (EC) cells]]** in the epithelium sample luminal chemistry and release **[[serotonin]] (5-HT)** onto nearby sensory nerve endings — an indirect, cell-relayed form of chemosensation.

steps.prompt: How do many gut afferents 'taste' the lumen if their endings don't reach it?
options: EC cells sample the lumen and signal to the afferent with serotonin
The afferent extends a long physical process directly into the open gut lumen
Goblet cells sample the lumen and release mucus onto the endings
The endings sense only stretch, which tracks what is in the lumen
steps.explanation: EC cells act as transducer cells: they face the lumen, detect chemicals, and release serotonin onto the afferent — a relay, not direct contact.

variants.setup: A sensory ending sits below the epithelium, not in the lumen.
variants.prompt: How can it still report luminal chemistry?
options: An EC cell relays the signal via serotonin
It pushes a process into the lumen
Goblet cells relay it via mucus
variants.reveal: EC cells sample the lumen and signal to the afferent with serotonin.

steps.setup: You block serotonin signaling between EC cells and afferents, then deliver a luminal chemical that EC cells detect.
steps.prompt: What do you predict for the afferent's response?
options: Blunted response to the chemical stimulus
Loss of its response to stretch instead
No effect, because afferents sense chemicals directly
steps.reveal: If EC-to-afferent serotonin is the relay, blocking it should blunt the chemical response — while leaving mechanical (stretch) sensing, a separate pathway, intact. This is why EC cells are studied as gatekeepers of visceral chemosensation.

options: Remove the stretch responses instead of these
variants.explanation: Serotonin is the EC→afferent relay for chemistry; blocking it blunts chemical responses.

sources.note: Enterochromaffin cells are gut chemosensors coupling to sensory nerves via serotonin.
